protections: Twig string callables passed to map/filter/reduce/sort/find/'has some'/'has every' are checked against a six-name PHP-function denylist (system, passthru, exec, file_get_contents, file_put_contents, popen) after lowercasing and stripping a leading backslash (src/web/twig/Extension.php:114-129, callers at 101, 110, 557, 574, 590, 715, 1194).
Craft's DI helper refuses a config array that specifies both '__class' and 'class' (src/Craft.php:54-61).
Html::dataUrl() confines file reads to the project root, excludes system directories, and rejects .php files (src/helpers/Html.php:987-1008).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: create() is a documented, first-class Twig function that site templates legitimately use; the existing guard covers PHP callables passed to filters, so create() looks like intended surface rather than a missing protection.
configure() only assigns properties/setters on objects a template can already reach and cannot instantiate a class, so it looks harmless once arbitrary class construction is blocked.

renderObjectTemplate() and craft.app.getView().renderString() are ordinary documented APIs; if the fix removes the dangerous function from the Twig environment, the re-entered render uses the same restricted environment and seems harmless.
The denylist lowercases and strips a leading backslash and already names the obvious RCE/file functions, so it reads as a finished check rather than a partial one.
Html::dataUrl() already enforces project-root containment, system-directory exclusion, and a .php ban, so the file-read helper looks fully hardened.
svg() only reads files whose MIME type is image/svg+xml, and the code explicitly says file paths are assumed safe, so it does not look like a file-disclosure route.

fairness_risks: create(), configure(), renderObjectTemplate(), dataUrl(), svg() and the map/filter/sort/find string-callable form are all documented Twig features; removing or denying them outright breaks legitimate site templates and title/URI formats that must keep working.
A restrictive Twig method/property policy on object templates would also block legitimate field accessors and query methods used by existing title and URI formats.
An allowlist for string callables in map/filter/sort would break legitimate uses such as |map('strtoupper'), |sort('strcmp') and |filter('trim').
Resolving symlinks/realpath in Html::dataUrl() would reject deployments that legitimately symlink asset volumes or storage into the project root.
Object templates legitimately contain {% ... %} tags and {field} placeholders, so stripping Twig tags or rejecting method access wholesale breaks conditional title formats.
Restricting the shared 'craft' global or the shared Twig Extension would affect both CP and site templates, not just the user-controlled object-template surface.

design.why: Three independent fix sites with different dismissal reasons. T1 (group T1/T2/T3) is the reported route: untrusted title/URI formats are rendered by View::renderObjectTemplate() in the full Twig environment, where create()/configure()/renderObjectTemplate()/craft.app re-entry all stay unguarded even after the arrow-callable denylist; its reason to dismiss is that these are documented Twig APIs. T4 is the existing guard's shape problem (string-only denylist, missing call_user_func/array_map/readfile-class callables and array callables), dismissed because the normalization makes the list look complete; this is the mimo-type how-mechanism. T5 (with T6) is the CWE-22 file-path route: Html::dataUrl()'s containment is lexical rather than realpath-based and svg() has no root/system-dir check, dismissed because dataUrl already has three checks. DeepSeek needs the documented-API dismissal in T1, MiMo needs the coupled/how-type checks in T4 and T5; no single edit closes all three groups.

unverified: The a_fix (e77f8a287dcd) and b_fix (e31e50849ad7) commits are not inspectable from the pinned worktree; the H3 classification is inferred from the only in-tree Twig-injection guard (checkArrowFunction, src/web/twig/Extension.php:114-129), which covers arrow-callable strings but not create()/configure()/object-template re-entry. If the A fix landed outside this 4.x tree, a_fix_leaves_b_open should be re-checked against the 5.x fix commit.

The candidate record labels the pattern 'H3u'; it was resolved to H3b (incomplete fix: B lives in Extension::getFunctions, not in the checkArrowFunction code) from the pinned evidence, not from the upstream diff.

create()'s arbitrary-class behavior and configure()'s property/setter behavior depend on upstream Yii BaseYii/Container code, which is not vendored in this worktree; the in-repo evidence is the function registration (src/web/twig/Extension.php:1418-1420), the inheritance chain (src/Craft.php:35, lib/yii2/Yii.php:15) and the re-implemented property assignment in src/helpers/App.php:1450-1455.

The array-callable and unlisted-callable bypasses of checkArrowFunction depend on Twig's CoreExtension::map/filter calling $arrow($value, $key); Twig is not vendored here, so the exact callable semantics were not executed.

The dataUrl symlink bypass requires a symlink inside the project root outside the system paths listed in src/services/Path.php:588-605; no in-repo route by which an unprivileged CP user can create such a symlink was proven.
svg() disclosure is limited to files whose MIME resolves to image/svg+xml (src/helpers/FileHelper.php:411-414); its practical impact was not demonstrated.
No reachable no-argument gadget for configure()-only escalation was proven in this tree; T2 is recorded as a missing protection rather than a demonstrated end-to-end RCE.
